title: Prove a cold first session registers on a small machine
text: Source tests prove the resident listens before it loads the evaluator; that a loading, never-listening or exiting resident holds the hook client no longer than the harness ceiling (5 seconds below the shortest harness hook timeout); that a cold load longer than YOKE_HOOK_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS is waited out inside that ceiling; that a resident still loading exits at once on SIGTERM; that a restart accepts a resident a live hook relaunched; and that a spent wait answers hook_budget_exhausted with yoke hook resident restart as recovery. yoke setup restarts the resident before the first harness session. The first live check on a 2 vCPU, 1 GB Linux test machine showed Codex ready on its first turn, then a later tool call refused with YOKE_HOOK_RESIDENT_TIMEOUT inside the 10-second evaluation budget, and yoke hook resident restart timing out while live hooks relaunched the resident; both are fixed in source. Still owed: a live check on that machine that Cursor's first turn after yoke setup registers its session, and that a first hook after the ten-minute idle retirement answers inside Cursor's 30-second hook timeout.
